text: Building and finishing an Update Set follows four steps, and the order genuinely matters here, not just as a formality. Set it Current, make your changes, review what got captured, then mark it Complete.

Step one: create or pick your Update Set in the picker at the top of the screen and switch to it before touching anything else. Step two: make your actual customizations -- ServiceNow captures each one automatically as you work, there's no separate save-to-Update-Set step to remember. Step three: review the related list of captured changes. Step four: mark it Complete once you're confident it's ready to move.

Here's the real, common beginner mistake worth flagging explicitly. An admin edits a Business Rule first, then creates a new Update Set afterward and switches to it. That edit already landed in whatever was previously current -- usually the system's Default Update Set -- not in the new one they meant to use. The fix isn't clever, it's disciplined ordering: switch first, edit second, every single time.

The Default Update Set exists as a catch-all so changes always land somewhere, even when an admin forgets to create a dedicated container. But it accumulates unrelated work across many sessions over time, and most teams never promote Default itself to another instance. If you find your own work sitting in Default, take that as a clear signal you skipped step one.

Before completing, review the Update Set's captured changes to catch two different problems: work you meant to include that's actually missing, and unrelated changes that quietly snuck in while this Update Set happened to be current. A single-purpose, cleanly scoped Update Set is far easier to promote and troubleshoot later.

Marking an Update Set Complete locks it as finished and ready to move -- a one-way step in normal practice, not something you keep editing afterward. Next up: how a Completed Update Set actually travels from one instance to another, step by step.
